findings.message: For a guard whose whole job is to stop a tampered response from redirecting the bearer token, `startswith("http")` is too weak a test for "absolute". It is case-sensitive, so "HTTP://attacker.example/..." skips the check entirely, and it misses scheme-relative "//attacker.example/...", which httpx resolves against the base URL's scheme and sends off-host. Decide on absoluteness from urlparse instead — e.g. treat the URL as absolute (and validate it) whenever it has a netloc, and reject any scheme that is not http/https.

`_authentication_provider` is private Kiota state and these are typing.cast calls, which do nothing at runtime. If the adapter was built with anything other than a bearer-token provider, `provider.access_token_provider` raises AttributeError and every paginated run breaks — and a Kiota rename turns the same code into a hard failure with no type-check warning. Please read the provider defensively (getattr / isinstance) and fall back to just self.allowed_netloc when the allowed-hosts list cannot be obtained.
